name: George H. W. Bush
summary: A Republican who campaigned as a conservative heir to Reagan, opposing abortion, taxes, drug legalization and gun-control limits, and favoring the death penalty, free trade and a strong defense. In office he signed the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Clean Air Act Amendments and a deficit-reduction deal that raised taxes, and he led the US through the end of the Cold War, the Panama invasion and the Gulf War through coalition diplomacy. He favored voluntary community service and market-based remedies over expanded government programs.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Rejected a nationalized health system as rationing care; proposed private-market reform with tax credits and insurance-market rules, and in 1988 declined to mandate employer coverage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said prosperity comes 'through free markets, free speech, free elections ... unhampered by the state' and applied market mechanisms to environmental rules.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Pledged no new taxes and in 1992 opposed raising taxes, preferring capital gains cuts and spending control. He did sign the 1990 budget deal tax increase, which he justified by deficit reduction.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Ordered a 90-day moratorium on new regulations that could hinder growth and urged clearing away 'high regulation, redtape'; backed market-based rather than command-and-control rules, while saying he supported 'sound regulations that serve the public good'.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inaugural lists welfare among things people are enslaved to, alongside drugs, yet he proposed no welfare cuts there and in 1988 said he wanted to help families off welfare; ambiguous.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Called talk of legalizing or decriminalizing marijuana and other drugs 'all wrong' and launched a national strategy built on enforcement.

state-harmful.rationale: Said 'I do not hate government. A government that remembers that the people are its master is a good and needed thing.'

limit-guns.rationale: Said free men and women should have the right to own a gun to protect their home, yet imposed the 1989 import ban on 43 firearm types and proposed limits on magazines over 15 rounds; resigned from the NRA in 1995 over its attacks on federal agents, not over gun policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: Proposed more than doubling federal aid to state and local law enforcement and more prisons, courts and prosecutors; also accepted defense cuts as the Cold War ended while refusing cuts that endanger a safe margin.

decide-locally.rationale: Said power 'must always be kept close to the individual' and that each level of society should do 'only what it does well, and no more'; called for returning power to families, communities, cities and States.

rehabilitation.rationale: Drug strategy stressed that offenders be 'caught, prosecuted, punished', more prisons and tough sentencing for kingpins, alongside expanded treatment.

traditional-family.rationale: Called the family 'the essential unit of closeness and of love' that communicates culture, faith and traditions to children.

abortion-legal.rationale: Backed a constitutional amendment protecting life with exceptions only for rape, incest and the mother's life; said his view had moved 'in favor of life'. Earlier he was pro-choice; the later position is used.

more-religion-public.rationale: Supported voluntary school prayer or a moment of silence and opened his presidency with a prayer.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Signed the ADA and the 1991 Civil Rights Act with remedies for discrimination and spoke of leaving 'the tired old baggage of bigotry', but vetoed the 1990 bill as a quota bill and rejected preferences.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Signed the Immigration Act of 1990, which increased legal immigration by about 40 percent, calling immigration 'a bridge to America's future'.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Said the Gulf crisis put the UN in sight of performing as its founders envisioned and worked through Security Council resolutions; did not call for transferring more power to it.

free-trade.rationale: Negotiated and signed NAFTA and pressed to 'break down the walls that stop world trade' and eliminate tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Stressed building a 'new partnership of nations' and said isolationism 'is no virtue', while insisting allies share burdens.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sent US forces to Somalia in 1992 to end mass starvation under UN authorization, though in the 1992 debate he was cautious about ground forces in Bosnia.

limit-growth.rationale: Said 'economic growth is the key to our endeavors' and in 1990 praised a clean-air law for balancing growth and environmental protection.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Said 'we must use clean, safe nuclear power' and more gas, coal and nuclear for the energy base.

military-superiority.rationale: Held to 'peace through strength' and refused defense cuts beyond a vital margin of safety, while accepting reductions after the Cold War.

school-vouchers.rationale: Backed parental school choice under America 2000, but sources opened do not describe public vouchers for any school.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Made deficit reduction a central aim, urged a five-year $500 billion reduction package and signed the 1990 budget deal.

national-self-determination.rationale: In Kiev he said 'freedom is not the same as independence' and favored good relations with both Gorbachev and the republics; ambiguous on a right to separate states.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Asked Congress for incentives for domestic oil and gas exploration and faster Alaskan energy development, alongside conservation.

national-mission.rationale: Described America as 'a unique nation with a special role in the world' and as an idealist leading toward a 'freer and more democratic planet'.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Described government as a part of the nation of communities, not minimal, and signed the ADA, Clean Air Act Amendments and Immigration Act, expanding its role.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Invoked 'all men are created equal' in signing the ADA and said freedom is an inalienable right of all men and women.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Defined democracy as government that 'derives its just power from the consent of the governed'.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Agreed with allies that an American military presence in Europe was essential and consulted NATO leaders.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: His administration played a key role in German reunification within NATO.

death-penalty.rationale: Supported capital punishment for crimes of extraordinary cruelty, for drug dealers who kill police and for drug kingpins.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Held that Iraq 'will not be permitted to annex Kuwait' and cited UN rejection of the annexation.

patriotic-education.rationale: Said public school teachers should be required to lead the Pledge of Allegiance.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Vetoed the 1990 civil rights bill as introducing quotas, said 'I don't believe in quotas', and sought employment protection 'without resorting to the use of unfair preferences'.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Signed the ADA, which he described as ending exclusion of disabled people from the mainstream, and the 1991 Civil Rights Act, which expands remedies against employment discrimination by private employers.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Said prosperity has a purpose and criticized those who treat wealth as an end in itself; called for helping the homeless and the disadvantaged.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Vetoed the 1990 bill over disparate-impact rules he said induce quotas, but signed the 1991 act that codified disparate impact with safeguards.

democratic-peace.rationale: Said in 1992 'Democracies ... don't go to war with each other' and called for promoting democratic impulses.

non-intervention.rationale: Ordered the invasion of Panama to remove Noriega and sent forces to Kuwait and Somalia; in Kiev he said the US would not meddle in internal affairs.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Kept the US in NATO and said US troops should stay in Europe.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Argued public money alone cannot end social problems and turned to voluntary community groups, the 'thousand points of light'.

term-limits.rationale: Proposed term limits for members of Congress in the 1992 debate and welcomed support for term limitation in 1991.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Ordered armed action in Panama (1989), led the Gulf coalition to reverse Iraq's annexation of Kuwait, and sent troops to Somalia, beyond defending US territory.

arms-reduction.rationale: Pursued arms-control agreements, negotiated cuts in US-Soviet forces and announced nuclear force reductions in 1992.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: In the 1992 debate proposed a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution and a line-item veto.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Said in 1988 he would not make unilateral cuts in strategic defenses while negotiating, though in 1992 he announced some unilateral reductions.

notes: Views changed over time: pro-choice and birth-control supporter in the 1960s-70s, he opposed abortion with narrow exceptions by 1980 and through his presidency (most recent position used). He called Reagan's tax plans 'voodoo economics' in 1980, pledged 'no new taxes' in 1988, then agreed to a 1990 budget deal with tax increases. Gun record is mixed (home-gun rights, 1989 import ban, 1995 NRA resignation over rhetoric). He reportedly said he voted for Hillary Clinton in 2016; no policy position follows from that. Civil rights record is mixed: vetoed the 1990 bill as a quota bill, signed the 1991 act and the ADA.
